verdict: Kimco's profit more than doubled to $272M, lifted by $89M of property-sale gains and record 96.6% occupancy, while rent revenue kept growing steadily.

kpis.label: Net income (common)
kpis.note: $0.41 per diluted share, vs $0.19 a year ago

segments.name: Rental property revenue
segments.note: Rent from grocery-anchored shopping centers and mixed-use properties — $539.7M, up from $531.1M a year ago, with same-property NOI up 4.9%.

segments.name: Management & other fees
segments.note: Management and other fee income — $6.4M in the quarter.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings over their lives — a large non-cash cost for a property owner.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company: head office, finance and legal.

opex.name: Impairment charges
opex.note: Write-downs on properties whose value fell.

otherDetail: Other income of $92M: an $89M gain on sales of properties (including The Witmer apartments), $74M of income from joint ventures and $13M of mortgage and financing income, minus $88M of interest expense and plus $3M of other income. Net income here is the $279M attributable to the company, after $3M attributable to noncontrolling interests and before $7M of preferred dividends (leaving $272M for common shareholders). As a REIT, Kimco's income tax was near zero ($0.1M).
oneTimers: Gains on sales of properties were $89M in the quarter, versus $4M a year ago — the main reason net income more than doubled. FFO, which excludes property-sale gains, was $316M ($0.47 per share).
Impairment charges were $8M in the quarter, versus $0.4M a year ago.
footerNote: Kimco reports operating income of $280M including the $89M gain on property sales; this chart shows that gain below the operating line (in Other income), so operating income here is $190M — total net income is unchanged. For a REIT, rent is the revenue, property taxes, operating and maintenance costs are the direct costs, and depreciation is the biggest running cost.

takeaways.title: Fullest centers on record
takeaways.text: Portfolio occupancy hit an all-time high of 96.6%, small-shop occupancy matched its record at 92.9%, and new leases signed at cash rents 31.5% above the old ones on comparable spaces.

takeaways.title: Property sales drove the profit jump
takeaways.text: Net income available to common shareholders rose to $272M ($0.41 per share) from $130M, mainly on $122M more of property-sale gains than a year ago, including selling The Witmer apartments for $211.5M.

takeaways.title: The rent engine grew too
takeaways.text: FFO — the REIT measure that strips out sale gains and depreciation — rose 6.8% per share to $0.47, same-property NOI grew 4.9%, and Kimco raised its full-year outlook again.
